chip_width.description: Fallback chip width in micrometers, at chip_baseline_num_qubits qubits, for topology families with no dedicated QPlacer-measured anchor (see _TOPOLOGY_FAMILY_ANCHORS_UM in ChipState.processor_config). Scaled by sqrt(num_qubits / chip_baseline_num_qubits) per processor for those families; heavy-hex/rigetti/xtree/grid use their own QPlacer anchor instead. NOTE: ChipState.processor_config's fallback branch only ever reads THIS key (chip_width) for both dimensions (chips are square there) -- chip_height below is not consulted by the active pipeline, but IS still read directly by src/legacy_rl/tests/test_defect_mask.py, so it is kept.

chip_height.description: Fallback chip height in micrometers. NOT read by the active pipeline (ChipState.processor_config's fallback branch reads chip_width for both dimensions -- see its description) -- kept only because src/legacy_rl/tests/test_defect_mask.py reads params.chip_height directly.

chip_baseline_num_qubits.description: Qubit count the chip_width/chip_height fallback baseline was calibrated for (used only by topology families without a dedicated QPlacer anchor). Chip area scales linearly with num_qubits (side length ~ sqrt(num_qubits)).

coupler_spectrum.description: coupler frequency spectrum in GHz [lo, hi]

qubit_anharmonicity_default_ghz.description: Fallback per-qubit transmon anharmonicity (E_C, negative) in GHz, used only when a processor's input JSON has no anharmonicity_ghz (e.g. legacy/random-heavy-hex processors). Real IBM backends supply per-qubit calibration values via database.py instead. Typical measured range: -0.31 to -0.34 GHz.

floorplan_candidate_count.description: Baseline number of candidate qubit layouts Floorplan._primary_layout samples (spectral/tree-aware/ring-aware initial coordinate + spring refinement) to minimize edge crossings, before falling back to the deterministic guaranteed-embedding path if none reach zero crossings / min spacing. Actual count is scaled by sqrt(num_qubits/27) (see _primary_layout's effort_scale). Ported unchanged from 01_mainref/src/core/globalplacement.py's floorplan_candidate_count -- no coupler-boundary term anymore (that scoring term was removed along with the coupler-boundary refinement steps FP no longer does; see Floorplan module docstring).

floorplan_planarity_mode.description: How Floorplan._place handles a non-planar coupling graph (zero-crossing single-layer layout is mathematically impossible for one) -- 'strict' raises NonPlanarError, 'crossover' extracts a maximal planar subgraph (maximal_planar_subgraph) and records the cut edges (ChipState.cut_edges) for out-of-plane routing (air bridges) later. No chip in the current benchmark pool is non-planar (verified 2026-08-28), so this only matters for future/larger topologies.

octagon_ring_aspect.description: Aspect ratio (width/height) of the local polygon template used by Floorplan's ring-aware initial layout (_ring_aware_initial_coordinate/_polygon_template) when the coupling graph has heavy-hex-style 8-qubit rings (_detect_octagon_rings). Ported unchanged from 01_mainref/src/core/globalplacement.py -- a layout tuning constant with no physical derivation, just a shape that empirically reduced crossings for ring topologies there.

num_threads.description: number of threads for parallel processing

save_log.description: whether to also write logs to a log/<timestamp>.log file (console output happens either way)

min_qubit_spacing_um.description: Qubit non-overlap floor (center-to-center, Chebyshev/L-infinity distance -- see Floorplan.min_pairwise_distance, core/floorplan.py) enforced by Floorplan. This is NOT a routing-clearance budget: it currently equals qubit_width/qubit_height exactly (400.0 == 400.0), i.e. it is the bare 'qubit bodies don't physically overlap' floor with zero slack for wiring. FP has no notion of coupler segments or their required width (meander_spacing_um etc.), so it cannot and does not reserve routing room here -- see core/floorplan.py's module docstring ('FP/GP 책임 분리') for why that space is GP's responsibility instead (GP places Coupler.segments via Coupler.region(), possibly needing to push qubits further apart itself if routing needs more than this floor leaves). Do not raise this value to carve out routing margin -- that re-couples FP to a concern it's designed not to know about. As a hard non-overlap floor, Floorplan does not relax it (no percentage tolerance) when checking whether a placement is acceptable; see core/floorplan.py's _SPACING_FP_EPS_UM for the (float-rounding-only, not a design margin) tolerance actually used.

connection_pad_width_um.description: TransmonPocket connection pad aperture width in micrometers (qiskit-metal: connection_pads.pad_width). Corresponds to the physical width of the coupler attachment pad on the qubit body.

substrate_epsilon_r.description: Substrate relative permittivity used in Coupler.l's CPW half-wavelength formula via eps_eff=(epsilon_r+1)/2 (a microstrip approximation -- see Coupler.l's docstring for the CPW caveat). Default 11.9 is the standard textbook value for silicon, and matches the epsilon_r default in /home/LabMember/ngchoi/research/qiskit_metal/transmon_draw2.py:27 (calc_half_wave_length). This is a tabulated material constant with real external physical grounding (unlike the removed coupler_phase_velocity_m_per_s), but there is no repo-internal measurement/citation for it beyond that reference script.

qubit_pad_inset_um.description: Inset (um) from the qubit pocket's y-boundary (+-qubit_height/2) to each connection port: off_y = qubit_height/2 - qubit_pad_inset_um (see Qubit.ports). Backed out from the previous hardcoded off_y=180 at qubit_height=400 (200-180=20) so ports scale correctly if qubit_height changes. NOTE: the original 180 has no traceable physical derivation, and transmon_draw2.py:99 hardcodes the same off_y=180.0 rather than deriving it from an inset either -- this reparametrization fixes the height-scaling bug but does not add new physical grounding.

meander_spacing_um.description: Effective CPW meander pitch (um) -- used by Coupler.region()/GlobalPlacement to size each coupler's FP-confirmed placement box (ChipState.coupler_regions) via required_wire_area = Coupler.l * meander_spacing_um. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 from 120 back to 40: 120 had been taken from qiskit-metal RouteMeander's meander=dict(spacing='120um') in /home/LabMember/ngchoi/research/qiskit_metal/transmon_draw2.py:227, reasoning that it 'matches the user's own qiskit-metal rendering script for internal consistency' (see the entry this replaced). That reasoning was wrong: transmon_draw2.py is a loose 5-qubit rendering DEMO whose spacing was picked for a clear, uncluttered picture at low qubit density, not calibrated against any real chip's actual routing density -- there is no evidence it reflects what an actual meander needs at this pipeline's qubit/coupler density (400um qubits, up to 127 of them). Reverted to 40, the value this repo's own predecessor (01_mainref, coupler_meander_pitch_um, since removed/replaced by this parameter) used successfully end-to-end, including its router achieving 0/624 crossings -- i.e. 40 is grounded in demonstrated pipeline behavior at real chip density, not a primary physical/literature source (no such source exists for either 40 or 120; see the removed coupler_meander_pitch_um entry's own history). Prefer 'value that worked in an actual full pipeline run at this problem's scale' over 'value borrowed from an unrelated demo' when neither is a cited physical derivation. Practical effect of 120->40: required_wire_area (and so each coupler's box size and Coupler.num_segments) shrinks by 3x, which is what let GlobalPlacement's coupler boxes actually fit around their qubit pairs without overlapping (see GlobalPlacement's 2026-09-17 box-overlap measurement).

segment_size_um.description: Square segment side length (um) for QPlacer-style coupler partitioning (see Segment, core/state.py). Taken directly from QPlacer's partition_size (ref/80_QPlacer/Qplacer/qplacer/qplacer_bm/qplacement_param.py:11, benchmark_params.json). QPlacer's own code has no comment or documentation justifying this value either -- no independent physical derivation exists anywhere.

gp_coupler_order.description: Order GlobalPlacement._place processes couplers in when laying out Coupler.segments -- 'shortest_first'/'longest_first' sort by straight-line port-to-port distance, 'random' shuffles with a fixed seed (0) for reproducibility. Motivated by 01_mainref's router, where shortest-first clearly beat longest-first (2/624 -> 0/624 routing failures) on the reasoning that short nets are boxed into a tight region with little detour room, while long nets have more slack and can still find space later. First measured (2026-09-17) under the old design where GP could expand a coupler's search region beyond Coupler.region() when it ran out of room: 0 failures for every strategy on every chip regardless of order (occupancy 59.97%-81.42% never got tight enough to starve anything, so the signal did not reproduce). Re-measured (2026-09-17, same day) after GlobalPlacement was changed to a hard 2-tier design -- GP now only places within ChipState.coupler_regions (FP-confirmed via Coupler.region(), snapped outward to the segment_size_um grid) and never expands, so a coupler with no free cells left in its own box now genuinely fails instead of spilling elsewhere. Under that hard-box design, total failures across all 6 chips: shortest_first 114/418 (27.3%), longest_first 115/418 (27.5%), random 116/418 (27.8%) -- still no meaningful difference between strategies. Diagnosis (see GlobalPlacement verification log): each coupler's own box has ample standalone capacity (5+ segments of spare cells beyond what Coupler.num_segments needs, once boxes are grid-snapped) -- the failures come from box-box contention where multiple couplers' boxes geometrically overlap (a real, measured occurrence: 0.13%-4.23% of box pairs per chip overlap, see coupler_regions overlap stats) and whichever coupler is processed later loses the contested cells. Because that contention is structural/geometric (driven by qubit density and coupling topology, not by which coupler happens to go first), reordering redistributes *which* couplers fail without changing *how many* fail -- consistent with both measurement rounds. Kept shortest_first as default: it is tied for best (not worse than the alternatives) in both rounds, is the cheapest of the three to compute, and matches the 01_mainref precedent for this problem class -- there is no evidence favoring longest_first or random over it. Reducing the ~27% failure rate itself is a separate problem (box sizing/negotiation, not ordering) left for a follow-up.
